summary: The Messaging milestone that shipped as PR #112 ('Messaging: thread subscriptions + Router push format', merged 2026-10-02 as dea647b5, released as v0.1.59). It began on 2026-09-29 as the thread-subscriptions design, after orchestrators missed Sidekick posts because board listens expired. The Lead designed it, an owner correction (relayed by the chief of staff) and a direct owner decision turned the push into a neutral locator, and two prerequisite PRs (#108 storage, #106 presence) merged first under two parallel Sidekicks. The owner then approved folding delivery and the Router push format into one PR, built by two Sidekicks (sidekick-push owning the PR, sidekick-subs the subscriptions lane) with an Opus xhigh reviewer as verifier. It stopped merged and released, with one open follow-up: the live S3/S5/S6 delivery-matrix cells were never verified and a post-release live check was owed.

args.text: Thread subscriptions replace `board thread listen` in a hard cutover. Design: a durable thread_subscriptions table with a backfill for open participants; a TargetPresence + LoadedOnly seam on the delivery routes; one ReaderDeliveryWorker per reader (quiet/cap timing, hold/wake/drop, restore on restart); subscribe, subscriptions, unsubscribe and wait replace listen. Owner-set defaults: auto-subscribe on join; deliver/poll/off and hold/wake/drop; 2 min quiet and 10 min cap per thread; 24 h lifetime, renewable; persisted. Lead's structural choices (authorship delegated by the owner): subscriptions never touch Acknowledged; an active subscription always implies a watch; durable per-root windows are written in the post transaction; window id and generation fence settlement. Why: orchestrators missed Sidekick posts because listens expired.

args.text: Owner decision (asked directly by the Lead): the subscription notice is a neutral locator. It supersedes the owner's earlier 'notice + title' answer and matches the relayed correction. One Router-authored line per due root, at most 20 roots and 2 KB per notice; each line carries only the Router's notice label, the root id, the activity range and the message count; a held notice adds 'held since <UTC>', a draining one 'thread resolved'. No bodies, summaries, titles, author names, fetch or ack instructions, or wording that claims owner authority. Delivered is the notified-through cursor per reader and root; Acknowledged moves only on explicit inbox acknowledge, so a notice cannot hide unread messages; a duplicate notice after a crash is harmless. `board thread wait` returns the same notice data.

args.text: #112 C2 DM delivery intent. (1) DM-kind push records persist the caller's delivery intent: mode auto, queue or steer, plus an optional generation guard (service epoch and generation); non-DM records carry none; decoded through domain types, failing closed, no CHECK. The router_pushes migration is new in this PR, so it is amended in place and no released format changes. (2) At send time a steer or guarded DM to a target that is not running is rejected with a short typed reason and nothing is held. (3) On restore the owner delivers with the stored mode and pinned precondition; a steer or guarded record meeting not-running, a generation mismatch or a race settles rejected, never held; auto and queue follow the hold rules (LoadedOnly); a DM attempted without an outcome settles outcome_unknown and is never re-sent. (4) Tests: send-time rejections; auto/queue held then delivered across a restart; the restart-gap case; an unknown stored value fails closed; board unavailable while DMs still hold and deliver. Owner of C2: sidekick-subs.

args.text: Independent review of #112 at 4021f79a: corrections required. F1: a closed Claude Code peer rejects Auto DMs (NoRoute) instead of holding them. F2: a failed hold write or retry mark leaves the reader wedged until restart. F3: one corrupt subscription row, or a failed DM recovery query, stops valid readers from restoring. F4: a stored DM delivery error must return outcomeUnknown with the push link and a published error kind. F5: obsolete message header exports remain. F6: interrupted attempted pushes are not settled, and superseded or ended held subscription records are not terminalized.
